newsitem.title: LATVIA: O/N RATES SEEN STABLE, LAT RISES AGAINST DOLLAR.
newsitem.headline: O/N RATES SEEN STABLE, LAT RISES AGAINST DOLLAR.

text.p: Overnight rates were seen staibilisng in the 3.50/4.50 percent range and the lat edged up against the dollar as banks snapped up lats to buy one-year bonds auctioned on Wednesday, dealers said on Friday.
Overnight rates slipped from 3.90 percent/4.90 percent on Thursday to 3.30/4.30 percent and were seen stabilising in the 3.50/4.50 percent range for the next week or more.

Dealers said they were not expected to rise any more in the short-term as the liquidity situation in the banking sector seemed fine and because the central bank's average repo rate now stands at four percent.
In forex markets, the lat rose from 0.5720/30 to the dollar on Thursday to 0.5700/05 on Friday.
Dealers said there was a strong demand for lats on Friday as banks sold dollars to buy 12 million lats worth of government bonds sold at Wednesday's T-bill auction.
The lat was also pushed up by the dollar's fall against the Japanese yen and sterling.

Dealers did not anticpate any sudden demand for dollars or lats next week on the lcoal market and said that in the short-term, the lat/dollar rate would depend on the dollar's performance against other currencies in the SDR basket to which the lat is pegged.
